newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise ignoring Lebed sacking.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise ignoring Lebed sacking.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Friday as traders ignored President Boris Yeltsin's dramatic sacking of Alexander Lebed on Thursday.
The Russian Trading system index of 24 shares rose by 1.47 percent to 180.41 on $20.23 million in volume.
Traders forecast a further rise until the middle of next week.
Alexei Goncharov, chief analyst at Russian Brokerage House, said shares rose when some traders shrugged off persistent, old rumours about Yeltsin's supposedly low hemoglobin levels.
"After the low hemoglobin rumours, brokers started taking profits and now they have decided to start buying, especially after Yeltsin's lively address on television," he said.
On Thursday, Yeltsin appeared on television to announce dramatically that he was firing security supremo Lebed for disruptive behaviour.
"He (Yeltsin) spoke so energetically that everyone believed that he really controls the situation in the country and that he would allow no more disorder in the Kremlin," Goncharov said.
He said Lebed's sacking had no impact on the market and that there were many foreign orders in the morning.
"Lebed had no impact when he was appointed and made no impact was was fired," he said.
Alexei Genkin, a trader from Alfa-Capital, said Western investors decided that Friday was a buying day because they did not expect any other news to push the market down.
Surgutneftegaz was traded at $0.428 after $0.420 on Thursday's close, UES rose to $0.0796 from $0.0780, Orenburgneft rose to $1.90 after $1.70 and LUKoil fell to $8.45 from $9.83.
